```{r}
#| include: false
# Exercise 1, part b: tick-all (extype: mchoice). The stem must say that at least one
# statement is true; the second Answerlist in the Solution marks each statement True. or
# False., in the same order. The data are read from the file part a ships.
```

```{r data, echo = FALSE, results = "hide"}
f <- "ssr-furniture.csv"
d <- read.csv(if (file.exists(f)) f else file.path(exams:::.exams_get_internal("xexams_dir_exercises"), f))
suppressMessages(library(car))
options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))
d$instruction <- factor(d$instruction); d$age <- factor(d$age)
fp <- function(p) if (p < .001) "< .001" else paste("=", sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p)))
full  <- Anova(lm(minutes ~ instruction * age, d), type = 3)
msRes <- full["Residuals", "Sum Sq"] / full["Residuals", "Df"]; dfRes <- full["Residuals", "Df"]
cellM <- tapply(d$minutes, list(d$instruction, d$age), mean)
# JASP's simple main effects: SS within each age group, tested against the full model's residual
simple <- do.call(rbind, lapply(levels(d$age), function(a) {
  ms <- anova(lm(minutes ~ instruction, d[d$age == a, ]))["instruction", "Mean Sq"]
  data.frame(age = a, F = ms / msRes, p = pf(ms / msRes, 1, dfRes, lower.tail = FALSE))
}))
sOf <- function(a, col) simple[simple$age == a, col]
Fint <- full["instruction:age", "F value"]; pInt <- full["instruction:age", "Pr(>F)"]
stopifnot(pInt < .001, full["instruction", "Pr(>F)"] < .001, sOf("18-35", "p") > .3,
          sOf("36-60", "p") < .001, sOf("61-80", "p") < .001)
```

Question
========
Run simple main effects of the type of instruction, for each age group.

Check the statement(s) that is/are true; at least one statement is true.

Answerlist
----------
* For participants aged 61-80, the type of instruction makes a significant difference in assembly time.
* For participants aged 36-60, the type of instruction makes a significant difference in assembly time.
* For participants aged 18-35, the type of instruction makes a significant difference in assembly time.

Solution
========
In JASP, Simple Main Effects with instruction as the simple effect factor and age as the moderator. Each test uses the residual mean square of the full model (`r sprintf("%.2f", msRes)` on `r dfRes` df).

```{r, echo = FALSE, comment = ""}
cat(paste(sprintf("age %s : F(1, %d) = %8.4f, p %s  %s", simple$age, dfRes, simple$F,
                  ifelse(simple$p < .0001, "< .0001", sprintf("= %.4f", simple$p)),
                  ifelse(simple$p < .01, "significant", "not significant")), collapse = "\n"))
```

For 61-80 and 36-60 year olds the type of instruction makes a significant difference, for 18-35 year olds it does not (*p* `r fp(sOf("18-35", "p"))`).

Lecture 17, slide 37 (Recap: simple main effects).

Answerlist
----------
* True.
* True.
* False.
